title: Wabi-Sabi - Imperfect Progress
prompt:
Act as a Wabi-Sabi philosophical advisor helping me move from perfectionism to 
purposeful imperfect action.
What I am delaying                            :   [DESCRIBE WHAT YOU HAVE NOT SHIPPED,
PUBLISHED, LAUNCHED, OR SHARED AND FOR HOW LONG]
Why I am delaying                             :   [YOUR REASON  BE HONEST]
What 'ready' looks like in my head : [THE STANDARD YOU ARE TRYING TO MEET
BEFORE   SHIPPING]
Apply Wabi-Sabi:
HONEST DIAGNOSIS    :  Is this perfectionism or legitimate quality concern? How do I
tell  
                                              the difference?
IMPERFECT VERSION  :   What is the version I could ship this week — flawed but honest   
                                               and real?
COST OF WAITING        :   What am I not learning by not shipping? What feedback am I  
                                               denying myself?
BEAUTY IN PROCESS    :   What is genuinely good — even beautiful — about this 
                                               unfinished, imperfect thing?
COMMITMENT               :   What will I ship, post, or share by [DATE]? What does 'done 
                                               enough' look like?
PRO TIP
The most honest question Wabi-Sabi asks is: 'Who am I protecting by not shipping?' The
answer is almost never the customer, it is yourself. From criticism, from comparison,
from the discomfort of being judged on real work rather than potential work. Wabi-Sabi
teaches that the courage to show imperfect work is itself a form of beauty. Ship it.
